The first initialization chooses the mode for all databases from that module. For a worker, pass `config: { useOldExtensionFunctions: false }` on its first message.
This release adds SQLite's native math functions and updates SQLite to **3.54.1**. Existing legacy math and string functions remain enabled by default, so existing query results are preserved.
See [the migration discussion](https://github.com/sql-js/sql.js/pull/647) and [SQLite's math function reference](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_mathfunc.html

CI covers all five WebAssembly variants, browser/worker distribution checks and the new export regressions. In the recorded same-runner comparison, exporting a 577.53 MiB database took 233 ms with 21 MiB WASM memory; a 108 MiB database also exported under an enforced 64 MiB WASM cap. Performance varies by environment.
- `Database.export()` now keeps the existing database connection open, preserving update hooks, custom functions and aggregates, prepared statements/cursors, PRAGMAs, TEMP objects, attached da

- Preserve columns named `__proto__` in `Statement.getAsObject()` and `Database.each()` while keeping ordinary object results.
- Track function registrations by SQLite's ASCII case-insensitive name and argument count, allowing scalar and aggregate overloads to coexist and be replaced independently.

This release adds single-file WebAssembly builds and updates SQLite from 3.49.1 to 3.54.0.
- Allocate SQL strings on the heap in `Database.run` and `Database.prepare`, fixing failures with SQL larger than the WebAssembly stack (#482, #639).
- Reset the worker database after close so subsequent requests can initialize a fresh database (#638).
- Retain npm trusted publishing with provenance, and retry transient SQLite source download failures.

- Added new `Conflict` and `Index` types. `Conflict` represents a [`conflict_target`](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-insert.html#SQL-ON-CONFLICT) in an `ON CONFLICT`. It can be either a named constraint (`ON CONSTRAINT`) or a an `Index`.
- Added `Index`. `Index` is a description of a unique index which PostgreSQL can use for *unique index inference*. This is an alternative to specifying an explicit named constraint in a `conflict_target`.
- Added preliminary support for PostgreSQL ranges.

- **Modular Controller-View Engine:** Decomposed the monolithic 1,949-line `dashboard.php` into 10 lazy-loaded data providers (`src/data/dashboard/`) and 10 isolated template partials (`src/pages/dashboard/`). Database query volume is reduced by ~75% per page view.
- **Configurable Auto-Sleep & Wake:** Automatically puts inactive Baileys sockets into low-memory standby (15s to 24h idle timeout) while auto-waking on outgoing dispatches.

- **Docker Ready:** Production-grade container with Supervisor running Apache & Node.js worker with automatic database migrations.
- **Asynchronous Queue & Anti-Ban:** Resilient MySQL delivery queue with humanized typing presence indicators (`composing`, `recording`) and randomized delays to protect your number.
- **Modern Management Dashboard:** Built with PHP 8.2+, Tailwind CSS, and MySQL / TiDB Serverless.
